# statnnet

`statnnet` provides model selection and regression-style summaries for small,
single-hidden-layer neural networks fitted with `nnet`. It can select an
unpenalised Gaussian model by information criterion or work from an existing
supported `nnet` fit.

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("andrew-mcinerney/statnnet")
```

## Basic workflow

The main workflow chooses the input terms and hidden-layer size from multiple
random starts, then adds diagnostics and regression-style summaries:

```{r data, message=FALSE}
library(nnet)
library(statnnet)

data("auto_mpg", package = "statnnet")
analysis_data <- auto_mpg
continuous_variables <- c(
  "mpg", "displacement", "horsepower", "weight",
  "acceleration", "model_year"
)
analysis_data[continuous_variables] <- lapply(
  analysis_data[continuous_variables],
  function(x) as.numeric(scale(x))
)
```

```{r selection, eval=FALSE}
selection <- select_nnet(
  mpg ~ displacement + horsepower + weight + acceleration +
    model_year + origin,
  data = analysis_data,
  max_size = 3,
  n_starts = 10,
  seed = 2026
)

selection
selection_path(selection)
model <- statnnet(selection)
```

An existing supported fit can also be augmented directly:

```{r example, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
set.seed(2026)
fit <- nnet(
  mpg ~ weight + model_year + origin,
  data = analysis_data,
  size = 1,
  linout = TRUE,
  decay = 0.1,
  Hess = TRUE,
  maxit = 1000,
  trace = FALSE
)

model <- statnnet(
  fit,
  data = analysis_data,
  response = "continuous"
)

model
anova(model)
```

`summary(model)` returns structured average observed-row predictive effects and
grouped Wald-type summaries. `pce()` and `plot()` provide finite-difference
partial covariate effects with delta-method or simulation uncertainty.

```{r pce, eval=FALSE}
summary(model)
pce(model, "weight")
plot(model, "weight")
plot_network(model, annotate = "p_value")
```

These summaries describe the fitted response function. They are conditional
on the chosen network and are not post-selection or causal inference.

## Citation

Run `citation("statnnet")` for formatted references and BibTeX entries. If you
use `select_nnet()` for input or hidden-layer selection, cite McInerney and
Burke (2025). If you use covariance estimates, Wald summaries, grouped tests,
or covariate-effect methods, cite McInerney and Burke (2026). Analyses using
both parts of the package should cite both papers.

## Inference and diagnostics

When a covariance matrix is available, the fitted Hessian has passed the
package's numerical checks. The method is intended for small, parsimonious
networks. `statnnet()` records the hidden-to-input size ratio and reports an
architecture diagnostic when the hidden layer is larger than the fitted input
layer.

Wald p-values and delta-method intervals are approximate and conditional on the
architecture, penalty, and local optimum.
